source.display_title: 06/09/2026 - Ricardo Ventura x Ben Byrne  — Follow Up

setter.evidence: No setter suffix in the title and no setter referenced on the call. The prospect had been following Trevor for about three weeks.

prospect.name: Ricardo Ventura
prospect.occupation: Works on the DCS control system for an oil refinery — industrial control and instrumentation. Desk-bound at his own office, 08:00 to 17:00 or 17:30, nine hours a day, having previously held more physically active roles.
prospect.family_status: Married with children — the eldest son prompted his original fitness turnaround. His wife cooks all household meals and they share a bank account. They have just finished building their own house.
prospect.training_background: No athletic base through high school or early college. Started weightlifting about four years ago at 210-215 lb after his first son was born, self-taught from research plus informal help from two or three friends who take bodybuilding seriously; got down to 180 lb and held it. Trained at least four times a week and tracked macros. Has been shifting toward a hybrid approach — calisthenics, bodyweight work, box jumps, higher-intensity cardio and functional movement. Sessions currently run 90 minutes to two hours. Stopped entirely for the last six months to build his house, drifted to 190-195 lb and let macro tracking lapse. No formal coaching ever.
prospect.medical: High cholesterol, which he describes as part genetic and part habitual — 'some of it is genetical. Some of it is simply habitual.' Improving it is one of his stated goals. No injuries, chronic pain or movement limitations: asked in passing whether he had any, he said 'I don't have any, no.' No medication, clinician or treatment mentioned, and the cholesterol was never followed up on.

signals: Self-directed and demonstrably capable — 'everything else after that has been empirical, self-taught, just trying to do research on my own, those sorts of things' — and it worked: 215 lb to 180 lb with no paid help

Explicitly benchmarked the price against a delivery model he knows and rates higher: 'you could expect something like this from a coach that's physically there watching you... it sounds a little steep by the fact that it's only a person kind of talking to you over the phone'
Named price as the sole thing holding him back — 'the price really would be the only thing leaning towards not doing it'
Interrogated the seller directly on whether he uses the product himself and what results it gave him, which is buyer-side due diligence rather than enthusiasm
Not the_optimizer despite the profile fit: price registered as a value barrier, not as a quality signal
Not the_rebuilder: the six-month lapse was a deliberate, finite trade-off for a house build, not a lost season, and it is already over

goals.text: Get back toward 175-180 lb from 191-195, with the emphasis on lean mass rather than the number
Build genuinely functional capability rather than gym strength — 'muscle is not going to help you if you're trying to play with your kids... run with them, crawl with them'
Develop core strength as an injury-prevention foundation — 'the core is the belt of your entire body... can prevent many of the issues like back problems'
Improve cardiovascular fitness so strength is not isolated — 'you can lift weights, and you can still try to go for a run and run out of breath'
Look better and feel pleased with himself in the mirror
Be the fitness role model his own parents were not — 'I don't want to grow up telling them, hey, fitness is important, and for them not to see that in my life'
Learn from formal coaching for the first time — 'I'm just looking for a little bit more of guidance'
Make fitness a whole-lifestyle habit rather than a gym block — 'not just hitting the gym and then leaving it there, not taking it with me wherever I go'
Cut training time down from the current 90 minutes to two hours a session

pains.text: Six months entirely out of the gym while building a house, with 15 lb regained
Nine hours a day seated after previously active roles — 'because at my own office and that sort of thing, I have to sit down a lot on a computer'
Sessions of 90 minutes to two hours are hard to fit around a nine-hour day and a young family
Macro tracking and food discipline lapsed alongside the gym — 'those sorts of things kind of fell through the cracks as well'
No formal foundation and everything self-taught — 'I didn't have a good foundation, like through high school and early college, I really didn't work out'
Has little control over his own nutrition since his wife cooks for the household
Fitness has stayed compartmentalised in the gym rather than becoming a lifestyle
Was not raised with fitness modelled at home and does not want to repeat that with his own children

objections.raw_quote: Well, I mean, it is a significant investment, if you ask me. For an investment of the last sort, I would have to consult with my wife, simply because we're of the mindset that, you know, what's mine is ours. You know, what's yours is ours. It's not really just my money.
objections.rep_response: Probed the mechanics ('Do you guys share a bank account or something like that?') and ran the belief check and the anticipated-obstacles question, which surfaced the guarantee concern. Did not run the rest of the play — no 'is there any reason she would not want you healthier', no separation of needing her input from asking permission, no deposit-with-refund fallback, and no follow-up call booked to include her.

objections.raw_quote: she would probably wonder how much of a guarantee, I guess you could say, would Trevor provide when it comes to results. I'm putting in the effort... can we somehow guarantee, yes, this is exactly what you're looking for.
objections.rep_response: Answered with a specific numeric guarantee: 'our guarantee is based off of, well, number one, we can't guarantee that you're going to do the work... but tangibly, the guarantee is losing 10% body fat and adding 20 pounds to your kettlebell lifts.' No terms, remedy, timeframe or conditions were stated, and no OE move was run.

objections.raw_quote: I think it would be more the fact that it's so upfront for something that's not necessarily the one-on-one and what the one-on-one actually mean like physically one-on-one. Like, you could expect something like this from a coach that's physically there watching you... it sounds a little steep by the fact that it's only a person kind of talking to you over the phone and not necessarily there with you.
objections.rep_response: Argued the case reasonably — frame-by-frame video review catching things an in-person coach misses, daily access versus a few sessions a week, qualifications and structure, teaching to fish rather than giving the fish. Never checked whether the reframe landed and never returned to price or terms afterwards.

objections.raw_quote: I guess you could say that the price really would be the only thing leaning towards not doing it, but other than that, from how you described the structure of it, it sounds efficient. It sounds like it would deliver, which I like.
objections.rep_response: Ran a genuinely good diagnostic — 'the price isn't like seeing the value of investing 6k, or is it more like 6k is a lot and you just don't have that much available?' — then, once told it was a value question, moved into a features comparison and never came back to money. No plan structured, no financing mentioned, no financial-picture questions.

objections.raw_quote: And so... that sounds like it's paid up front?
objections.rep_response: Deflected to a credit card without disclosing that instalment plans or third-party financing exist: 'Well, a lot of our clients just throw it on a credit card and then, you know. They kind of make the payments there? Yeah.'

offer.guarantee_mentioned: Stated as a guarantee with figures and no terms: 'we can't guarantee that you're going to do the work, I mean, keep you accountable, but tangibly, the guarantee is losing 10% body fat and adding 20 pounds to your kettlebell lifts, which is usually coming with building lean muscle.'

evidence: Deferred to his wife with no decision: 'I would have to consult my wife, make sure that she's on board... and I would get back to you like that.'
No payment, no payment link sent — the rep described one ('I have a link they could just send over to you') but never dropped it.
No follow-up call booked; the agreed next step was a text or email from the rep and an answer from the prospect at some point.
Positive signal: conditional commitment stated twice — 'I can assure you that if I pay $6,000, I will be committed' and 'if we make the investment, I definitely commit to it.'
Counter-evidence: the value objection about remote versus in-person coaching was never resolved, and he named price as the only thing pulling him away.
Counter-evidence: the guarantee question raised on his wife's behalf was answered with unwritten figures, which is exactly the kind of answer that does not survive being repeated to a spouse.
outcome.next_step: Rep to send a text introducing himself; prospect to discuss with his wife and reply either way. No follow-up call scheduled and no payment link sent.

notable.note: Asked point blank what guarantee exists, and was told 'the guarantee is losing 10% body fat and adding 20 pounds to your kettlebell lifts' — the same two figures the rep presented as average results on 07 June and as 'the whole goal' on 08 June. Three framings of the same numbers in four days, and here it was the framing given to a man who was taking it to his wife. He also asked directly whether the rep uses the product himself and got a detailed personal results story. Best legacy question in the batch appeared on this call — 'Were your parents like that?' — answered 'No, they were not. And that's why I'm trying to make the change', and it was then never used against the price. Genuine value objection left open: he compared remote coaching unfavourably to the in-person coaching two friends of his provide, and nobody closed that loop.

quality.notes: Persistent swapping throughout, with several long inversions. 'When I first started, it was because my wife and I had our first son' at 00:02:35 is labelled to the rep but is the prospect; the whole block from 00:13:00 to 00:14:14 runs both speakers under alternating wrong labels including the rep's questions inside prospect turns; and the exchange at 00:44:15-00:44:52 puts the prospect's 'Is this a product, a service that you yourself would consume?' and the rep's answer under mixed labels. Roles resolved from content. Weight recorded as 193 as the midpoint of his own range, 'somewhere in between 191, 195'; he had not weighed himself recently. Body fat never measured or estimated. Number of children never established beyond 'kids' and 'our oldest'.
